The primary election took place on September 10, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Incumbent [[Rhode Island Democratic Party|Democratic]] Senator [[Sheldon Whitehouse]] was re-elected to a fourth term in office, defeating [[Rhode Island Republican Party|Republican]] state representative [[Patricia Morgan]] by a 20.05% margin. Whitehouse swept all five of the state's counties for the third consecutive time in his Senate career, and he overperformed [[Kamala Harris]] in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Rhode Island|concurrent presidential election]] by around 4.4 percentage points. Even so, his 20.05% margin marked a decline from his previous margins in [[2012 United States Senate election in Rhode Island|2012]] and [[2018 United States Senate election in Rhode Island|2018]], and this race was the closest in his senatorial career since his first election in [[2006 United States Senate election in Rhode Island|2006]]. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== *[[Sheldon Whitehouse]], incumbent U.S. senator{{cite news |url=https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2023/2/22/2154247/-Morning-Digest-Wisconsin-liberals-get-the-foe-they-want-for-crucial-Supreme-Court-contest#3 |title=Morning Digest: Wisconsin liberals get the foe they want for crucial Supreme Court contest |quote=Democratic Sen.
